- GIVEN an admitted child kind requires provider dispatch and no provider service is supplied
- WHEN the factory prepares the child session
- THEN construction MUST return a typed missing-service outcome
- AND it MUST NOT inspect ambient credentials, provider files, global registries, or environment values.

### Requirement: Child authority is a monotonic intersection

r[agent_harness_runtime.child_session_service.authority] Before construction, effective child authority and budgets MUST intersect parent policy, child profile, request ceilings, workspace scope, model and tool grants, depth, fan-out, time, token, turn, and result limits.

#### Scenario: A child requests a wider workspace

r[agent_harness_runtime.child_session_service.authority.workspace]
- GIVEN a child request names a workspace scope wider than its parent grant
- WHEN child admission runs
- THEN admission MUST deny creation with the widening source identified
- AND no session, store, provider, tool, or workspace effect may occur.

### Requirement: Child lifecycle and lineage are durable safe facts

r[agent_harness_runtime.child_session_service.persistence] The host MUST persist safe child identity, parent lineage, generation, lifecycle state, session head, result identity, and failure class through explicit store services while private child bodies remain in child-owned private channels.

#### Scenario: A non-terminal child is restored

r[agent_harness_runtime.child_session_service.persistence.restore]
- GIVEN restart finds a valid non-terminal child record and matching current services
- WHEN child restore admission runs
- THEN it MUST reopen the child through coding-session recovery using the recorded generation and session head
- AND it MUST not repeat committed provider or tool effects.

### Requirement: Parent results are bounded and typed

r[agent_harness_runtime.child_session_service.results] Collection MUST return a typed bounded child result with terminal class, safe lineage, content identity, and admitted model-visible body, without importing the full child transcript by default.

#### Scenario: A child result exceeds its limit

r[agent_harness_runtime.child_session_service.results.oversized]
- GIVEN a completed child result exceeds the admitted parent result limit
- WHEN collection projects the result
- THEN it MUST return a typed bound outcome or approved bounded summary
- AND it MUST NOT expose the excess body through receipts, events, or diagnostics.

### Requirement: Concrete child service evidence is adversarial

r[agent_harness_runtime.child_session_service.verification] The child service MUST include production-entrypoint tests for lifecycle success, cancellation, restart, lineage, result projection, missing services, stale handles, foreign parents, authority widening, bounds, malformed context, race outcomes, leak rejection, and dependency isolation.

#### Scenario: The child service is ready to archive

r[agent_harness_runtime.child_session_service.verification.closeout]
- GIVEN maintainers intend to sync and archive the child service
- WHEN focused and lifecycle validation runs
- THEN subagent, coding-session, store, recovery, RLM, receipt, dependency, Cairn, and relevant Nix checks MUST pass
- AND automatic delegation, remote workers, sandboxing, child correctness, task success, and production readiness MUST remain non-claims.

### Requirement: Committed kernel state has a private durable journal

r[agent_harness_runtime.steel_kernel_restore.journal] Animus MUST represent committed Steel kernel cells with versioned private records that bind source, ordered captured host results, clear markers, compatibility identities, bounds, and a BLAKE3-chained committed head.

#### Scenario: A bridged cell commits

r[agent_harness_runtime.steel_kernel_restore.journal.commit]
- GIVEN a bridged Steel cell reaches a successful final value
- WHEN the durable host commits its kernel record
- THEN the private record MUST bind the source and ordered result bodies to safe identities
- AND the safe ledger MUST contain only bounded metadata, identities, counts, and status classes.

### Requirement: Kernel replay performs no host effect

r[agent_harness_runtime.steel_kernel_restore.replay] Restore MUST rebuild a fresh kernel by replaying committed cells with host execution disabled and by supplying the exact captured result for each recorded bridge call.

#### Scenario: Restore replays a prior file-read result

r[agent_harness_runtime.steel_kernel_restore.replay.no_effect]
- GIVEN a committed cell used one captured file-read result
- WHEN a fresh process restores the kernel
- THEN replay MUST supply the recorded bounded result to the cell
- AND it MUST NOT call a file, process, tool, network, context, or child executor.

#### Scenario: Replay requests an unrecorded effect

r[agent_harness_runtime.steel_kernel_restore.replay.mismatch]
- GIVEN replayed source issues a request that has no exact ordered captured result
- WHEN the replay driver handles that request
- THEN restore MUST fail closed with a typed mismatch
- AND no host effect or partially restored kernel may become active.

### Requirement: Restore admission binds exact compatibility facts

r[agent_harness_runtime.steel_kernel_restore.admission] Restore MUST require matching session, kernel generation, Steel cohort, RLM policy, bridge schema, journal schema, and committed chain-head facts before replay.

#### Scenario: The Steel cohort changed

r[agent_harness_runtime.steel_kernel_restore.admission.cohort_drift]
- GIVEN a journal was committed under another Steel cohort
- WHEN restore admission evaluates the journal
- THEN admission MUST return a typed compatibility denial
- AND it MUST NOT attempt best-effort replay or silently clear the kernel.

### Requirement: Restore uses committed cell safe points

r[agent_harness_runtime.steel_kernel_restore.safe_points] Durable kernel heads MUST advance only at complete committed cell boundaries, and interrupted cells MUST remain explicit recovery outcomes whose completed external effects are not rerun.

#### Scenario: The process exits during a cell

r[agent_harness_runtime.steel_kernel_restore.safe_points.interrupted]
- GIVEN the prior kernel head is committed and the next cell is interrupted after one observed effect
- WHEN restart recovery runs
- THEN restore MUST activate only the prior committed kernel head
- AND active-turn recovery MUST retain the interrupted effect observation without rerunning it.

### Requirement: Kernel restore evidence is metadata-only

r[agent_harness_runtime.steel_kernel_restore.evidence] Kernel restore receipts MUST exclude source bodies, result bodies, prompts, credentials, private paths, and raw diagnostics while binding safe compatibility identities, chain heads, counts, outcomes, and required non-claims.

#### Scenario: A receipt draft includes source code

r[agent_harness_runtime.steel_kernel_restore.evidence.leak]
- GIVEN a restore receipt draft contains model-written source or a captured result body
- WHEN receipt validation runs
- THEN validation MUST reject the draft without echoing the private material
- AND the receipt MUST NOT contribute to readiness or release claims.

### Requirement: Durable kernel restore has adversarial evidence

r[agent_harness_runtime.steel_kernel_restore.verification] Durable restore MUST include production-entrypoint tests for successful replay, clear markers, captured results, effect suppression, wrong identity, cohort drift, policy drift, missing and extra results, order mismatch, corruption, interrupted cells, bounds, and leaks.

#### Scenario: The restore change is ready to archive

r[agent_harness_runtime.steel_kernel_restore.verification.closeout]
- GIVEN maintainers intend to sync and archive durable kernel restore
- WHEN focused and lifecycle validation runs
- THEN Steel, bridge, store, recovery, repair, receipt, Cairn, and relevant Nix checks MUST pass
- AND mid-cell restore, VM serialization, effect rollback, encrypted storage, power-loss immunity, and production durability MUST remain non-claims.

### Requirement: The RLM executor is an explicit non-default host

r[agent_harness_runtime.rlm_host_executor.boundary] Animus MUST provide the complete RLM host executor only as a non-default authority-scoped component with explicit route bindings, capability roots, command profiles, services, limits, and current authority facts.

#### Scenario: The executor is constructed

r[agent_harness_runtime.rlm_host_executor.boundary.explicit]
- GIVEN a host supplies exact bindings for the selected RLM operation classes
- WHEN executor construction validates the bindings
- THEN it MUST return one explicit executor with stable binding identities
- AND reusable and default crates MUST gain no filesystem, process, network, credential, persistence, or child authority.

### Requirement: Every operation uses its owning capability pack

r[agent_harness_runtime.rlm_host_executor.dispatch] The executor MUST route each admitted operation to its exact bound capability pack and MUST recheck current seal, generation, cancellation, scope, and binding identity before the effect.

#### Scenario: A required capability pack is absent

r[agent_harness_runtime.rlm_host_executor.dispatch.missing]
- GIVEN an admitted request names an operation with no bound pack
- WHEN executor dispatch runs
- THEN dispatch MUST return a typed unavailable outcome before the effect
- AND it MUST NOT use standard-library, environment, current-directory, shell, or global-registry fallback behavior.

### Requirement: Workspace operations remain capability-relative

r[agent_harness_runtime.rlm_host_executor.workspace] File reads MUST use an explicit capability root with lexical admission and no-follow observation, and file edits MUST use the existing revision-gated workspace edit host.

#### Scenario: A file changes before edit publication

r[agent_harness_runtime.rlm_host_executor.workspace.conflict]
- GIVEN an admitted edit binds an observed revision and target
- WHEN the current target no longer matches that revision
- THEN the workspace route MUST return a typed conflict before publication
- AND it MUST NOT overwrite, retry against a new revision, or widen the target scope.

### Requirement: Shell requests use exact bounded command profiles

r[agent_harness_runtime.rlm_host_executor.process] Shell-class requests MUST resolve to exact admitted command profiles with explicit argv, environment, root, input, output, deadline, cancellation, and teardown limits before bounded process execution.

#### Scenario: A command does not match a profile

r[agent_harness_runtime.rlm_host_executor.process.unknown]
- GIVEN a shell request cannot resolve to an exact admitted command profile
- WHEN process-route admission runs
- THEN it MUST deny the request before process creation
- AND it MUST NOT pass the request to an ambient command shell.

### Requirement: Tool, context, child, and clear routes retain their owners

r[agent_harness_runtime.rlm_host_executor.services] Named tools, context reads, child requests, and kernel clears MUST delegate to their existing application owners through explicit bindings without service discovery or authority duplication.

#### Scenario: A context result exceeds its model-visible limit

r[agent_harness_runtime.rlm_host_executor.services.context_bound]
- GIVEN an explicit context resolver returns more content than the admitted result limit
- WHEN the executor translates the result
- THEN it MUST return a typed bound outcome without exposing the excess content
- AND safe receipts MUST contain only bounded labels, counts, identities, and status classes.

### Requirement: Complete executor conformance covers every route

r[agent_harness_runtime.rlm_host_executor.verification] The executor MUST include positive and negative production-entrypoint tests for every operation class, current rechecks, service absence, capability denial, conflicts, process limits, cancellation, timeout, result bounds, failure translation, fallback rejection, receipt safety, feature isolation, and license isolation.

#### Scenario: The executor change is ready to archive

r[agent_harness_runtime.rlm_host_executor.verification.closeout]
- GIVEN maintainers intend to sync and archive the RLM executor
- WHEN focused and lifecycle validation runs
- THEN bridge, tool, workspace, process, context, child, receipt, dependency, license, Cairn, and relevant Nix checks MUST pass
- AND sandboxing, hermeticity, effect correctness, reversible mutation, task success, and production readiness MUST remain non-claims.

### Requirement: OpenAI tool projection preserves canonical meaning

r[agent_harness_runtime.tool_capable_openai_host.projection] The non-default OpenAI host MUST project admitted canonical tool declarations, assistant tool calls, and correlated tool results without dropping required roles, schemas, identities, or output controls.

#### Scenario: The model requests steel_repl

r[agent_harness_runtime.tool_capable_openai_host.projection.steel_repl]
- GIVEN a canonical request declares the admitted `steel_repl` tool and its exact schema
- WHEN the OpenAI host projects the request
- THEN the wire request MUST preserve the declaration name, description, schema, and tool-selection policy
- AND no tool execution may occur inside the provider adapter.

#### Scenario: A required field is unsupported

r[agent_harness_runtime.tool_capable_openai_host.projection.lossy]
- GIVEN a canonical request requires a field that the reviewed OpenAI cohort cannot preserve
- WHEN request projection runs
- THEN projection MUST fail before network contact with a typed unsupported-feature outcome
- AND it MUST NOT silently remove or downgrade the field.

### Requirement: OpenAI streaming uses the production parser

r[agent_harness_runtime.tool_capable_openai_host.streaming] The host MUST parse bounded SSE chunks through one deterministic production entrypoint that emits ordered canonical content, reasoning, tool-call, usage, finish, cancellation, and failure frames.

#### Scenario: Tool arguments arrive in multiple events

r[agent_harness_runtime.tool_capable_openai_host.streaming.tool_delta]
- GIVEN a provider stream contains ordered argument fragments for one tool call
- WHEN the production parser processes the chunks
- THEN it MUST emit correlated ordered tool-call frames and one bounded completed call
- AND malformed, duplicate, or over-limit fragments MUST fail closed.

### Requirement: Provider and tool correlation is exact

r[agent_harness_runtime.tool_capable_openai_host.correlation] Provider continuation requests MUST match the Animus model-call identity, provider response identity, provider tool-call identity, committed assistant call, and supplied tool result before network contact.

#### Scenario: A tool result names another call

r[agent_harness_runtime.tool_capable_openai_host.correlation.mismatch]
- GIVEN a continuation carries a tool result for a stale or different provider call
- WHEN correlation admission runs
- THEN admission MUST reject the continuation before transport
- AND no result may enter another response chain.

### Requirement: Capability negotiation precedes contact

r[agent_harness_runtime.tool_capable_openai_host.capabilities] The host MUST negotiate requested tool, stream, reasoning, usage, role, and budget requirements against exact selected-model capability metadata before transport.

#### Scenario: Tool calls are not supported by the selected model

r[agent_harness_runtime.tool_capable_openai_host.capabilities.denied]
- GIVEN a request requires tool calls and selected-model metadata does not admit them
- WHEN capability negotiation runs
- THEN dispatch MUST fail closed before credential or network use
- AND the host MUST NOT switch models, endpoints, or providers automatically.

### Requirement: Network and credential authority stays in the host shell

r[agent_harness_runtime.tool_capable_openai_host.authority] Endpoint selection, credential values, HTTPS transport, deadlines, response bounds, cancellation, and failure observation MUST remain in the non-default authority-scoped host shell.

#### Scenario: No explicit credential is supplied

r[agent_harness_runtime.tool_capable_openai_host.authority.no_credential]
- GIVEN an admitted tool-capable request has no explicit credential value or approved credential service result
- WHEN the host prepares transport
- THEN it MUST return a typed missing-credential outcome
- AND it MUST NOT inspect ambient provider files, accounts, keychains, or environment values by default.

### Requirement: Tool-capable provider evidence is bounded

r[agent_harness_runtime.tool_capable_openai_host.verification] The host MUST include positive and negative production-parser fixtures, projection tests, correlation tests, capability tests, fake transport tests, authority tests, leak tests, dependency isolation, and separately classified optional live evidence.

#### Scenario: The provider change is ready to archive

r[agent_harness_runtime.tool_capable_openai_host.verification.closeout]
- GIVEN maintainers intend to sync and archive the tool-capable host
- WHEN focused and lifecycle validation runs
- THEN provider, projection, streaming, capability, runtime-event, retry, receipt, Cairn, and relevant Nix checks MUST pass
- AND live reliability, tool safety, task success, arbitrary endpoint support, broad provider parity, and production readiness MUST remain non-claims.

### Requirement: Steel skill modules bind reviewed source and exports

r[agent_harness_runtime.steel_skill_modules.descriptor] Animus MUST represent an optional Steel skill module with exact manifest, frozen-source, language-cohort, source-body, export, dependency, capability, trust, bounds, and domain-separated BLAKE3 identities.

#### Scenario: A trusted module descriptor is valid

r[agent_harness_runtime.steel_skill_modules.descriptor.valid]
- GIVEN a selected skill binds one complete bounded Steel source unit, named exports, exact dependencies, and an admitted capability ceiling
- WHEN descriptor validation runs
- THEN it MUST return a stable module identity and safe summary
- AND the descriptor alone MUST NOT evaluate source or grant host authority.

### Requirement: Module admission precedes Steel evaluation

r[agent_harness_runtime.steel_skill_modules.admission] The host MUST validate source identity, trust, language cohort, syntax class, imports, exports, bounds, and effective policy before staged module evaluation.

#### Scenario: A module requests a native import

r[agent_harness_runtime.steel_skill_modules.admission.native_denied]
- GIVEN a module imports an unreviewed native module, dynamic library, arbitrary path, or package-manager reference
- WHEN module admission runs
- THEN admission MUST reject the module before evaluation
- AND it MUST NOT search the host, filesystem, network, environment, or package registry.

### Requirement: Module dependencies resolve deterministically

r[agent_harness_runtime.steel_skill_modules.dependencies] Module dependency resolution MUST be pure over supplied descriptors and MUST reject cycles, missing identities, duplicate modules, version conflicts, export conflicts, trust violations, capability widening, and cumulative bound overflow.

#### Scenario: Two modules export the same name

r[agent_harness_runtime.steel_skill_modules.dependencies.export_conflict]
- GIVEN two selected modules export one name without an explicit reviewed alias
- WHEN dependency resolution runs
- THEN resolution MUST fail with a deterministic conflict
- AND no module may enter the staged kernel.

### Requirement: Skill effects use the normal Steel bridge

r[agent_harness_runtime.steel_skill_modules.authority] Steel skill code MUST request host effects only through existing resumable bridge operations under the intersection of session, profile, skill, and current host capabilities.

#### Scenario: A skill requests an undeclared tool

r[agent_harness_runtime.steel_skill_modules.authority.tool_denied]
- GIVEN a loaded skill calls a named tool outside its declared or effective capability set
- WHEN bridge admission processes the call
- THEN it MUST deny the call before executor dispatch
- AND the skill MUST NOT register a new host operation or use an ambient fallback.

### Requirement: Module lifecycle uses kernel safe points

r[agent_harness_runtime.steel_skill_modules.lifecycle] Module loads and removals MUST occur only through explicit staged kernel transitions, and committed module identities MUST survive compaction and bind durable effect-disabled replay.

#### Scenario: Module initialization fails

r[agent_harness_runtime.steel_skill_modules.lifecycle.atomic]
- GIVEN a selected module fails during staged initialization
- WHEN the loader reaches the error
- THEN it MUST discard all staged definitions from that load operation
- AND the prior committed kernel and module set MUST remain authoritative.

### Requirement: Steel skill module evidence covers unsafe paths

r[agent_harness_runtime.steel_skill_modules.verification] Module support MUST include positive and negative production-entrypoint tests for descriptors, policy, dependency order, exports, bridge use, safe points, compaction, restore, untrusted source, drift, cycles, conflicts, native imports, capability widening, bounds, partial loads, and leaks.

#### Scenario: The module change is ready to archive

r[agent_harness_runtime.steel_skill_modules.verification.closeout]
- GIVEN maintainers intend to sync and archive Steel skill modules
- WHEN focused and lifecycle validation runs
- THEN skill, source, profile, Steel, bridge, restore, receipt, dependency, Cairn, and relevant Nix checks MUST pass
- AND native modules, package installation, automatic activation, skill correctness, task success, and production readiness MUST remain non-claims.
